personality.buyer: Administrators, IT teams, MSSPs, and network security managers responsible for firewall monitoring, compliance, and incident investigation
personality.reasoning: Firewall Analyzer is an infrastructure security product, so the visual language should feel precise, controlled, and credible. The brand palette from Techjockey is already orange-led, so I use it as the system accent while keeping the overall experience security-first with a dark, authoritative hero and clean operational sections. The layout should communicate live monitoring, log intelligence, and compliance through dashboards, rule-based panels, and proof-oriented cards rather than decorative marketing visuals.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is 9 words long, so 48px keeps it strong while preventing awkward line breaks on desktop and preserving hierarchy on smaller screens.

colours.colourReason: All colour choices are derived exclusively from the supplied Techjockey brand palette. The primary orange becomes the hero background and CTA colour, white provides clean contrast, near-black supports security authority, and soft grey creates separation between sections without introducing outside brand tones.

layout.heroReason: A split hero allows the product to feel operational and premium: copy on one side, a layered firewall dashboard visual on the other. The orange hero ties directly to Techjockey branding, while the right-side visual can show log streams, alert cards, and monitoring panels in a PNG UI mockup.
layout.featureReason: The content is naturally grouped into a primary capability set, a why-choose value set, and an additional benefits set. A spotlight section for the strongest capability followed by structured grids makes the product easier to scan and creates stronger contrast between consecutive sections.
layout.darkSectionFor: hero only, with optional dark diagnostic panel accents inside feature callouts if needed

personality.imageryDirection: Use a layered cybersecurity dashboard composition with firewall log timelines, live monitoring cards, bandwidth graphs, and alert badges. The visual should feel like an actual administrator console with floating metric chips, not abstract marketing art. If a screenshot is unavailable, build a CSS-based UI shell with tabs, counters, and console-style panels. Keep iconography precise, technical, and square-edged.
personality.designPersonality: Controlled, analytical, and confident. The page should feel like a security operations cockpit: structured grids, sharp spacing, subtle shadow depth, live-data cues, and proof-driven messaging. It should communicate that firewall monitoring is simplified without looking playful or generic SaaS; instead it should feel dependable, premium, and highly technical.

layoutStrategy.hero: Use a strong full-width dark security hero with centered or slightly split text treatment depending on available product imagery. Keep the CTA prominent and singular, with the subheadline supporting fast time-to-value and network security outcomes.
layoutStrategy.features: Follow a single-column page flow with repeated feature modules. Each section should have a clear intro, then grid-based cards with moderate spacing and high scanability. Avoid carousel, tabs, or accordion interactions.
layoutStrategy.proof: Use testimonials as the primary trust layer since there are no badges, awards, or social proof stats. Keep proof lightweight but credible, with role and industry context visible.
layoutStrategy.pricing: No pricing module should be introduced. Maintain a lead-generation posture through product value communication and CTA continuity.
layoutStrategy.form: No form section should be added in this build because includeForm is false. CTAs should route to the existing conversion path without introducing a dedicated lead form block.
